rows.title: Highlander
rows.evidence: Wikipedia page names the work and the island. Image is an open photograph of the island location named in the article.
rows.summary: Highlander is a 1986 fantasy action-adventure film and the first installment in the Highlander franchise. The scene in which the MacLeod clan sets off to battle is supposed to take place "in the village of Glenfinnan, on the shore of Loch Shiel" in the Lochaber area, but was actually filmed at Eilean Donan Castle, which is in the same general area but is really on the shore of Loch Duich, a sea loch near Kyle of Lochalsh and the Isle of Skye.

rows.summary: The Vanishing, previously titled Keepers, is a 2018 British psychological thriller film directed by Kristoffer Nyholm and written by Celyn Jones and Joe Bone. Based on the 1900 disappearance of the Flannan Isles Lighthouse crew, it stars Gerard Butler, Peter Mullan, and Connor Swindells as three lighthouse keepers whose shift takes a dark turn. Three men begin their six-week shift tending to the remote Flannan Isles Lighthouse.

rows.title: The Invasion of the Isle of Wight
rows.evidence: Wikipedia page names the work and the island. Image is an open photograph of the island location named in the article.
rows.summary: The German occupation of the Channel Islands during the Second World War essentially by-passed Herm. The island was claimed on 20 July 1940 by Nazi Germany, a few weeks after the arrival of German troops in Guernsey and Jersey; German soldiers landed on the island to shoot a propaganda film, The Invasion of the Isle of Wight.

rows.title: Walk Me Home
rows.evidence: Wikipedia page names the work and the island. Image is an open photograph of the island location named in the article.
rows.summary: Inch Kenneth (Scottish Gaelic: Innis Choinnich) is a small grassy island off the west coast of the Isle of Mull, in Scotland. The island was a location for the 1993 feature film Walk Me Home produced by author Timothy Neat.

rows.title: Father Ted
rows.evidence: Wikipedia page names the work and the island. Image is an open photograph of the island location named in the article.
rows.summary: Father Ted is a sitcom created by Irish writers Graham Linehan and Arthur Mathews and produced by British production company Hat Trick Productions for British television channel Channel 4. The opening sequence (including shots of the Plassy shipwreck) were filmed over Inisheer — the smallest of the Aran Islands.

rows.title: When Eight Bells Toll
rows.evidence: Wikipedia page names the work and the island. Image is an open photograph of the island location named in the article.
rows.summary: When Eight Bells Toll is a 1971 British action film directed by Étienne Périer and starring Anthony Hopkins, Jack Hawkins, Robert Morley, and Nathalie Delon. It was done partly on location on and near the Isle of Mull in Scotland, including Tobermory, Dervaig, Bloody Bay, Rubha nan Gall lighthouse, Duart Castle, and Fingal's Cave.

rows.title: The Guard
rows.evidence: Wikipedia names The Guard and Lettermore, the English name of Leitir Móir, as a filming location. Image is an open photograph of Lettermore.
rows.summary: The Guard is a 2011 buddy cop comedy film written and directed by John Michael McDonagh, starring Brendan Gleeson, Don Cheadle, Mark Strong and Liam Cunningham. Principal filming began on 29 October 2009, in Lettermore County Galway. Filming took place over a six-week period in Connemara, Lettermore, Lettermullan, Spiddal, and Barna with some scenes for filming in Wicklow and Dublin.

rows.title: Macbeth (1971 film)

rows.summary: Macbeth was filmed in various locations around the British Isles, starting in Snowdonia in Wales in October 1970. A considerable amount of shooting took place in Northumberland on the northeast coast of England, including Lindisfarne Castle, Bamburgh Castle and beach, St. Aidan's Church and North Charlton Moors near Alnwick.

The film was set and partially filmed on the island of Steep Holm.

rows.title: Arthur Scott Robertson
rows.evidence: Wikipedia names the fiddler and his birth on Bressay.
rows.summary: Arthur Scott Robertson (15 February 1911 – 6 February 2000) was a fiddle player from Shetland. Born in Bressay and raised in Nesting, he was first introduced to the instrument by his neighbor Willie Hunter Snr.

rows.title: The Homes of Donegal
rows.evidence: The song's article names the ballad and says its writer was a native of Cruit Island.
rows.summary: The Homes of Donegal is an Irish ballad written by songwriter Seán McBride in 1955. McBride was a native of Cruit Island which is in The Rosses area of north-west County Donegal.

rows.title: Thíos Cois na Trá Domh
rows.evidence: The Cruit Island article says the song originates from the island.
rows.summary: Cruit Island (Irish: An Chruit or Oileán na Cruite) is a small inhabited island in the Rosses district in the west of County Donegal in Ulster, the northern province in Ireland. The song Thíos Cois na Trá Domh originates from the island and remains a popular song in the Donegal Gaeltacht to this day.

rows.title: Amhrán na Trá Bháine
rows.evidence: The Gorumna article names the caoine and the village of Trá Bhán on the island.
rows.summary: During the 1860s in South Boston, Massachusetts, Bríd Ní Mháille, an immigrant from the Gorumna village of Trá Bhán, composed the Irish-language caoine, Amhrán na Trá Bháine, which is about the drowning of her three brothers, whose currach was rammed and sunk while they were out at sea.

rows.title: Inisheer
rows.evidence: The Inisheer article names the slow air after the island.
rows.summary: Inisheer is also the name of a well-known slow air written by Thomas Walsh from Dublin, after a visit to the island in the 1970s.

rows.title: Lasairfhíona Ní Chonaola
rows.evidence: Wikipedia calls her a singer-songwriter and places her home on Inis Oírr.
rows.summary: Lasairfhíona Ní Chonaola (Irish pronunciation: [ˈl̪ˠasˠəɾʲˌiːnˠə]; born c. 1977), known mononymously as Lasairfhíona, is an Irish singer-songwriter. She is deeply rooted in the sean-nós singing style of her home on Inis Oírr, one of the Aran Islands.

rows.title: Wa'ney Island Cockfight
rows.evidence: The Walney Island article names the song and places the cockfight on the island.
rows.summary: In music, Walney appears in the song "Wa'ney Island Cockfight", which describes a cockfight between the lads of North Scale and Biggar on the island.

rows.title: Darach Ó Catháin
rows.evidence: Wikipedia names the sean-nós singer and his birth at Maimin, Lettermore, which is Leitir Móir.
rows.summary: Darach Ó Catháin (30 September 1922 – 29 September 1987) was an Irish sean-nós singer. Ó Catháin was born on 30 September 1922 at Maimin, Lettermore, Connemara seventh in a family of twelve children.

rows.title: My Love's in Germany
rows.evidence: The song's article names the melody and places its composer, Thomas Traill, on Papa Westray.
rows.summary: "My Love’s in Germany" (My Luve's in Germanie) is a poem written by Scottish poet Hector Macneill. It was first printed in 1794 and is the lament of a Scottish woman for her lover. The song was re-published in 1885 by Colonel David Balfour as an Orkney melody composed by Colonel Thomas Traill around 1630. Traill (from Holland Farm, that is "the farm on the high land", in Papa Westray), was a soldier in the army of Gustavus Adolphus, also known as Germany Thomas, during the Thirty Years' War.

rows.title: Skerryvore
rows.evidence: The band article says Skerryvore formed in Tiree in 2000. The lighthouse they are named after is a reef offshore, so the row is filed on Tiree. Image is an open photograph of the band.
rows.summary: Skerryvore are a Scottish Celtic rock band originally formed by Daniel Gillespie and Fraser West in Tiree, Argyll and Bute in 2000, after the two began playing ceilidh music together at various functions. Named after the Skerryvore lighthouse which lies 12 miles (19 km) off the coast of Tiree, the band have released six studio albums, a compilation album, and a live album.

rows.title: The Hut on Staffin Island
rows.evidence: The Staffin Island article names the tune.
rows.summary: Staffin Island, also known as Stenscholl Island or Fladdaidh, is an uninhabited islet in Staffin Bay, off the east coast of the Trotternish peninsula of Skye in Scotland. "The Hut on Staffin Island" is a tune composed by Phil Cunningham.

rows.title: Moladh Ulbha
rows.source_title: Ulva in literature and the arts
rows.evidence: The Ulva article names the song In Praise of Ulva.
rows.summary: Moladh Ulbha (In Praise of Ulva) is a song written by the Ulbhach Bard, Colin Fletcher (Cailean Mac an Fhleisdeir).

rows.title: "Peerie" Willie Johnson
rows.evidence: Wikipedia names the guitarist and his birth on Yell.
rows.summary: "Peerie" Willie Johnson (William Henry Johnson) (10 December 1920 in Yell, Shetland – 22 May 2007 in Lerwick, Shetland) was a Scottish folk guitarist and bassist. He was respected as an influential and innovative musician in the Shetland folk scene.
